adminAi.semanticDescription: Includes datasets whose meaning is close to the query even without keyword matches.

adminAi.summaryDescription: A resource is described automatically as it is registered. This is for the ones that predate the setting, and for rewriting what another model, prompt version or language produced. External URLs are not fetched. It spends on inference in proportion to the number of resources. Each resource's embedding is rebuilt as its description is written.
adminAi.summaryLocaleHint: The language descriptions are written in from now on. Existing ones are not rewritten; to rewrite them, save and then run Rewrite all.
adminAi.summaryLocaleSaved: Saved. It can take up to a minute to apply.
adminAi.summaryFillScope: Writes descriptions only where there is none yet.
adminAi.summaryRefreshScope: That, and rewrites the descriptions another model, prompt version or language produced.

adminSite.title: Site Management
adminSite.registrationDescription: Whether new users can sign up from the sign-up page. While off, system administrators create users from the user management screen. Changes take effect within a minute.

What each key is for is up to whatever displays it, so agree on the keys with whoever built the brand. Keys starting with kukan- are reserved for KUKAN itself.
adminSite.metadataPublic: Every value is readable by anyone through the public API. Enter only values that may be public.
adminSite.metadataDelay: Visitors who are not signed in see a change up to about 90 seconds after it is saved. Signed-in users see it sooner.

versionBackfill.backfillDescription: {count} resource(s) do not have a version yet. This records each resource's current file as v1 (no re-fetch or re-indexing). It is a one-time migration step and disappears once complete.
versionBackfill.backfillQueued: Backfill queued. This section disappears once it completes.

rowGroupBackfill.title: Prepare tables for BI tools
rowGroupBackfill.description: {count} tables have not been checked for serving to BI tools (Excel, Tableau and the like). Checking lets tables with many columns or long text be served as well. Nothing is fetched from the source again.
rowGroupBackfill.reinterpret: Up to {count} of them need their file rebuilt. That is done from the stored copy, so nothing is fetched for those either.
rowGroupBackfill.queued: Queued. This item disappears once it completes.

searchAnalysis.title: Re-analyse the search index
searchAnalysis.description: The search analysis settings have changed (such as the Japanese analysis, or how formats are matched regardless of case). Analysis is fixed when an index is created, so the change reaches this deployment only by rebuilding it. The stored text is re-read in place — nothing is fetched and no file is processed again. This is a one-time step after an upgrade, and it disappears once it is done.
searchAnalysis.queued: Re-analysis queued. This notice goes away once it finishes. Anything saved while it runs is brought in again when it finishes.

contentChunks.title: Rebuild the content search index
contentChunks.description: The content of {count} resources is in the search index in the larger units used before. Search now reads content in smaller units, so rebuilding makes content search and passage search lighter. It works from the stored files — nothing is fetched from the publisher again. It indexes again from the stored interpretation, so files are not interpreted again (except where the interpretation has not caught up with the file). Until its turn comes, each resource still turns up in dataset search as it is indexed now (passage search finds it once it is rebuilt). This item disappears once it is done.
contentChunks.queued: Queued. The resources are rebuilt one by one and the count goes down as they are. This item disappears once it completes.

embeddingBackfill.title: Regenerate embeddings
embeddingBackfill.description: {count} resources are outside semantic search. Regenerating brings them back within reach of searches whose keywords do not match. No external URL is fetched and no file is reprocessed. This item disappears once it completes.
embeddingBackfill.queued: Queued the embedding regeneration. It proceeds in the background, and this item disappears once it completes.

resource.odataKeyRemovable: You can remove that column in the BI tool.
resource.odataKeyOwn: The primary key {columns} identifies each row. No column is added.
resource.odataKeyAdded_not-designated: This table has no primary key set, so a {column} column holding the row’s position is added — OData requires a key.
resource.odataKeyAdded_key-missing: The column the primary key names is not in the table as it stands, so a {column} column holding the row’s position is added.
resource.odataKeyAdded_key-float: The primary key rests on a Number (floating-point) column, which cannot identify a row, so a {column} column holding the row’s position is added.
resource.odataKeyAdded_unsafe-integers: The primary key holds integers large enough that a reader can lose their last digits and take two rows for one, so a {column} column holding the row’s position is added.
resource.odataKeyAdded_key-null: The primary key has missing values, so a {column} column holding the row’s position is added.
resource.odataKeyAdded_key-not-unique: The primary key repeats, so a {column} column holding the row’s position is added.
resource.odataKeyAdded_unverified: A composite key is checked as the version is taken in; until that lands, a {column} column holding the row’s position is added.
resource.odataUnavailableColumns: This table's headings contain characters an OData identifier cannot hold (brackets, spaces, punctuation, periods), so it is not served yet. Headings at fault: {columns}
resource.odataUnavailableDuplicate: Two or more columns share a name, so this table is not served. Headings at fault: {columns}
resource.odataUnavailablePrivate: Only resources of public datasets are served.
resource.pipelineStatusDescription: Check the processing status of this resource and re-run the pipeline.
resource.pipelineNoNewVersion: No new version — the file matches the content already stored
resource.actionFailed: That did not go through. Reload to see the current state before trying again.

versions.title: Version history
versions.purgeWarning: This makes the version unobtainable. Its file is deleted.
versions.purgeCaseLive: This version is what the resource is serving now, so the preview and the search index go with it — serving falls back to v{fallback} and both are rebuilt from that version’s content.
versions.purgeCaseLiveLast: This version is what the resource is serving now, and there is no version left to fall back to: the resource is left with no file, and nothing is rebuilt.
versions.purgeCaseNotLive: This version is not what the resource is serving. What is being served, its preview and its search index are unchanged.
versions.purgeCaseMayMove: That describes the resource as it is right now. Serving can move before you confirm — another run publishing, or a revert — in which case the deletion follows whatever is live then.
versions.purgeWarningTail: If you need this version’s content, download it first. Whichever case this is, rows may remain in versioning’s internal storage, where deletion is not guaranteed (history retained for other resources can reference the same files). Where storage versioning is enabled, the superseded object expires after its retention window (30 days by default). This cannot be undone.
versions.reasonPlaceholder: Reason for the deletion (recorded in the audit log)
versions.diffSchemaChanged: The columns changed, so a row-level diff is not available.
versions.purgeWarningSameContent: Other versions hold the same content ({versions}). Deleting this one does not erase it, and the resource may go back to serving that version’s copy. Delete them individually if they must go too.

diffUnavailable.purged: One of the versions has been deleted, so a diff is not available.
diffUnavailable.no-previous-version: This is the first version, so there is nothing to compare against.
diffUnavailable.not-ingested: v{version} has no row-level snapshot, so there is nothing to compare against. Where a reason was recorded, the version list shows it.
diffUnavailable.key-missing: A key column is not in v{version}, so its rows cannot be identified and no diff is available. Correcting the key applies from the next version on.
diffUnavailable.key-null: A key column of v{version} has empty values, so its rows cannot be identified and no diff is available. Correcting the key applies from the next version on.
diffUnavailable.key-not-unique: The key of v{version} does not identify a row, so no diff is available. Correcting the key applies from the next version on.
diffUnavailable.ingest-failed: Loading v{version} for row-level diffs failed repeatedly, so no diff is available.

noTable.out-of-memory: Ran out of memory interpreting it
noTable.ragged-rows: rows do not split into the same columns
noTable.not-records: Not a list of records, so there is no table

columnSettings.title: Primary key
columnSettings.loadError: Could not load the column settings
columnSettings.noColumns: No columns have been interpreted yet. They become selectable once the pipeline has run.
columnSettings.willClear: Applying removes the primary key. From then on, editing one row shows in a diff as one row added and one removed.
columnSettings.willApply: Applying creates one version, and versions from there on are ingested under this key.
columnSettings.carried: The current version is ingested under this key.
columnSettings.pending: Set, but no version has been ingested under it yet.
columnSettings.queued: Applied. A rebuild is queued to create the version ingested under this key.
columnSettings.queueFailed: Applied, but the rebuild could not be queued — no version will be read under this key until one runs. Use “Queue the rebuild” to try again.

fault.key-missing: That column is not in the current content. As it stands, a version ingested under this key would be left out of diff ingestion.
fault.key-null: A column of this key has empty values. As it stands, a version ingested under this key would be left out of diff ingestion.
fault.key-not-unique: This key does not narrow a row down to one. As it stands, a version ingested under this key would be left out of diff ingestion.
fault.key-float: A Number column holds a floating-point value, which cannot identify a row — so this key cannot be applied.

unchecked.no-preview: The current content could not be read, so whether this key narrows a row down to one could not be checked. Applying still works.
unchecked.preview-stale: The interpretation has not caught up with the current content, so whether this key narrows a row down to one could not be checked. Applying still works.
unchecked.retyped: A key column will be read as another type or in another format, so the current values cannot say whether this key identifies a row. You can still apply it.

columnSettings.rebuildQueued: The rebuild is queued. It takes a few minutes; the sample appears the next time this is opened after it finishes.
columnSettings.confirmCost: Applying creates one version, but that version is left out of diff ingestion, so no diff involving it can be shown — not even rows added and removed. Correcting the key later does not bring it back in, because a past version’s diff is not changed after the fact. If the content that arrives next satisfies this key, versions from there on are ingested.
columnSettings.noCounts: This version does not record per-column duplicate and empty counts, so nothing can be marked unique — it was interpreted before those were kept. Choose and check, or rebuild the interpretation.
columnSettings.floatNotKeyable: A column of type Number cannot be used in a primary key: a floating-point value is approximate, and a value written out is not guaranteed to read back as itself, so the same row cannot be matched by the same value across versions. To key on such a column, choose Integer as its type for values without a fraction, or Decimal for values with one (a decimal keeps the digits as written). A key set before the column was read this way keeps working, but it does not identify a row either.
columnSettings.recommendKey: If a column holds an identifier that stays with each row (a ward code, a facility number), setting it as the primary key is recommended: diffs between versions then show which rows changed. Applying a change of primary key creates one version.

guide.summary: About types, the primary key and roles
guide.keyWhat: The column (or columns together) that identifies each row of the table.
guide.keyDiff: Here it matches the same row between two versions, so a diff can count "changed rows".
guide.keyNone: Without one, a rewritten row shows as one row removed and one added.
guide.rulesLead: The chosen columns (together, if several) must meet all three of these. If they do not, the reason is shown before you apply.
guide.rulePresent: The column is in the content
guide.ruleUnique: No two rows share a value
guide.ruleUniqueMark: A column marked "unique" meets all three on its own.
guide.ruleFloat: Number (floating-point) columns cannot be used: the value is approximate, and is not guaranteed to read back as written. Settled as Integer or Decimal, they can.
guide.stableLead: This cannot be checked in advance. Choose columns where the same row always keeps the same value, and a value always stays with the same row.
guide.stableRenumber: Numbers reassigned at every release: unchanged rows show as removed and added.
guide.stableReuse: Retired numbers reused for something else: unrelated things show as one changed row.
guide.stableNone: If those are the only columns, leaving the primary key unset is safer.
guide.rolesLead: A role decides how a column's values are used in search and shown on the public page. Roles are decided from the values and the column name, and the table shows why.
guide.rolesListed: {roles}: values listed and used in search
guide.rolesFree: {roles}: used in search as text, with the row for context
guide.rolesOverride: A text column's role can be chosen again. No version is made, and applying takes it in by reprocessing. A column read as a number or date has its role from its type.
guide.typesLead: What a column's values are read as. It is inferred from the values; where the inference is wrong, settle it.
guide.typesUse: A code whose leading zeros matter as String; an amount or a rate whose digits must stay exact as Decimal.
guide.typesFormat: A Date or Datetime also takes the way the file writes it (the format). Auto decides it from the values, and reads the column as text where the day and month order cannot be told.
guide.typesFailures: A value the settled type cannot read is read as no value, and the column shows how many with examples. No row is dropped.
guide.typesVersion: A type changes how the file is read, so applying it creates a version. Going back to Auto does too.

columnSettings.rolesWillApply: Changing a role makes no version. Applying rebuilds the profile and the search index by reprocessing.
columnSettings.rolesQueued: Applied. A reprocess to take in the roles is queued.
columnSettings.previewStale: A preview would be of the previous content, so none is shown — the interpretation has not caught up with what the resource is serving.
columnSettings.rolesIntro: A column's role decides how its values are used in full-text search. A text column's role can be chosen again; each option says what it does in search.

roleSearch.auto: Use the role decided from the values and the column name
roleSearch.identifier: Not used in search (codes, numbers, URLs and the like)
roleSearch.numeric-text: Not used in search (numbers mixed with values that do not read as numbers)
roleSearch.name: Searchable by value (facility or place names: many different values)
roleSearch.category: Searchable by value, and put beside free-text sentences as the row's context (kinds, types)
roleSearch.free-text: Searchable as one sentence per row, with the row's category values beside it (remarks, descriptions)

columnSettings.rolesPending: The role changes are not in the profile and the search index yet. They are once the run finishes; if it does not move, "Queue the rebuild" starts it again.
columnSettings.typesWillApply: A type changes how the file is read, so applying makes a version. Values the settled type cannot read are left empty, and the column says how many.

columnSettings.castFailures: Values that could not be converted: {count} (read as no value)
columnSettings.typesIntro: A column can be read as a type you settle instead of the inferred one — a code column as text to keep its leading zeros, an amount or a rate as a decimal. Changing a type and applying makes a version.
columnSettings.formatNote: The format is how the file writes the values. A month, day or hour without its leading zero reads too (2026/8/8 7:05).
columnSettings.castFailuresEstimate: Of the first {rows} rows, {count} ({percent}) are expected not to convert (they would read as no value). The preview outlines them in red
columnSettings.castFailuresEstimateWhole: Of {rows} rows, {count} ({percent}) are expected not to convert (they would read as no value). The preview outlines them in red
columnSettings.noFailuresEstimate: The first {rows} rows are expected to read
columnSettings.noFailuresEstimateWhole: Every value is expected to read
columnSettings.dateUndecidedEstimate: The values are not expected to tell whether the day or the month comes first, so the column would read as text. Choose a format.
columnSettings.formatEstimate: Left to the values, the format is expected to be {example}
